# 0.1 Create a Phyloseq Object with .qza files

```{r}
physeq_O <- qza_to_phyloseq(
  features = "filtered-table-genus.qza",
  tree = "tree/rooted_tree.qza",
  taxonomy = "taxa.qza",
  metadata = "metadata.tsv"
)

physeq_O
```

## Remove Archaea and Eukaryota

```{r}
## https://www.biostars.org/p/9513395/
physeq_OF <- subset_taxa(physeq_O, Kingdom !="d__Archaea")
# physeq_OF
physeq_OF <- subset_taxa(physeq_OF, Kingdom !="d__Eukaryota")
physeq_OF
head(tax_table(physeq_OF))

taxa <- tax_table(physeq_OF)
write.csv(taxa, "taxa_phyloseq.csv")
```

## Read the data and create phyloseq objects

```{r}
otu_mat <- read_excel('OTU_matrix.xlsx') # OTU table
tax_mat <- read_excel('Taxonomy_table.xlsx') # Tax table
samples_df <- read_excel('Samples.xlsx') # Samples - metadata

# Define the row names from the OTU column
otu_mat <- otu_mat %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("OTU")

# Idem for the two other matrices
tax_mat <- tax_mat %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("OTU")

samples_df <- samples_df %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("SampleID")

# Transform into matrixes otu and tax tables
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_mat)
tax_mat <- as.matrix(tax_mat)

# Transform and creating a Phyloseq Object
OTU = otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
TAX = phyloseq::tax_table(tax_mat) # https://github.com/joey711/phyloseq/issues/1597
samples = sample_data(samples_df)

physeq_M <- phyloseq(OTU, TAX, samples)
physeq_M
```

## Removing Archaea and Eukaryota

```{r}
## https://www.biostars.org/p/9513395/
physeq_MF <- subset_taxa(physeq_M, Kingdom !="Archaea")
### physeq_MF
physeq_MF <- subset_taxa(physeq_MF, Kingdom !="Eukaryota")
physeq_MF

## Visualize data
sample_names(physeq_MF) #samples

rank_names(physeq_MF) #Taxonomy

sample_variables(physeq_MF) #variables
```

# 0.3. Normalization

```{r}
# To normalize the number of reads in each sample using median sequencing depth
# With this, physeq_N is different to physeq_OF
# Fundamental for the PCoA plots and differential abundance testing

total = median(sample_sums(physeq_MF))
standf = function(x, t=total) round(t * (x / sum(x)))
physeq_N = transform_sample_counts(physeq_MF, standf)
physeq_N
```

# 1. Rarefaction Curves

```{r}
## https://fromthebottomoftheheap.net/2015/04/16/drawing-rarefaction-curves-with-custom-colours/ (Important)
## https://micca.readthedocs.io/en/latest/phyloseq.html (2nd important)

## Set the file for the results
setwd("~/Escritorio/R/2026_COPROFAGIA/coprofagia/1_Rarefaction_curves")

tab <- otu_table(physeq_MF)@.Data
class(tab) #it has to be a matrix (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74530039/error-vegan-rarecurve-error-in-asx-matrixi-j-drop-false-subscript)
rarecurve(t(tab), step=50, cex=0.5)
#### Save as "Rarefaction_curve_simple.png"

raremax <- min(rowSums(t(tab)))
raremax
col <- c("black", "darkred", "forestgreen", "orange3", "blue", "hotpink")
lty <- c("solid", "dashed", "longdash", "dotdash")
rarecurve(t(tab), step = 20, col = col, lty = lty, label = TRUE)
#### Save as "Rarefaction_curve_samples_colors.png"

write.csv(tab, "sample_size_per_species.csv", row.names=FALSE)
```

## 1.1. Sample size per groups

```{r}
# Generate and load the function generate_grouped_xlsx
source("generate_grouped_xlsx.R") 
generate_grouped_xlsx(
  counts_input = "1_Rarefaction_curves/sample_size_per_species.csv", 
  metadata_input = "Samples.xlsx",
  output_name = "1_Rarefaction_curves/sample_size_per_groups.xlsx"
)

tab_groups <- read_excel('1_Rarefaction_curves/sample_size_per_groups.xlsx') 
raremax2 <- min(rowSums(t(tab_groups)))
raremax2

# High-contrast colors
group_colors <- c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02")
# Distinct line textures: 1 = solid (CON), 2 = dashed (SCP), 5 = long-dash (CP)
group_line_types <- c(1, 2, 5)

# Set label = FALSE to clean up the overlapping text boxes from the plot
rarecurve(t(tab_groups), step = 20, col = group_colors, lty = group_line_types, label = FALSE)
abline(v = raremax2)

# Add a clean, non-overlapping legend in the bottom-right corner
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"), 
       col = group_colors, 
       lty = group_line_types, 
       lwd = 2.5, 
       bty = "n")
# Save as "Rarefaction_curve_groups_colors.png"
```

## 1.2. Generate the faceted plot

```{r}
# 0. Re-order the group factors within the phyloseq object
physeq_MF@sam_data$group <- factor(physeq_MF@sam_data$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# 1. Generate the base rarefaction curves
p_rare_base <- ggrare(physeq_MF, step = 50, color = "group", label = "Sample", se = FALSE)

p_rare <- p_rare_base +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"), breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"), breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# 2. Add the Facet Layer to separate by group
p_faceted <- p_rare + 
  facet_wrap(~group, ncol = 3) + # This creates 3 side-by-side columns
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"),
                     breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP")) +
  theme_bw() +                  # Clean white background for publications
  labs(
    x = "Sequence Sample Size", 
    y = "Species Richness", 
    title = "Rarefaction Curves per Group"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90"), # Labels on top of each plot
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

# 3. View and save the plot
print(p_rare)
print(p_faceted)
ggsave("1_Rarefaction_curves/Rarefaction_faceted_groups.png", p_faceted, width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## 1.3. Venn Diagram of Shared ASVs

```{r}
# 1. Merge samples by group to see presence/absence per group
group_merged <- merge_samples(physeq_MF, "group")

# 2. Identify the list of ASVs present in each group
# We consider an ASV present if its count is > 0 after merging
asv_list <- list(
  CON = colnames(otu_table(group_merged))[otu_table(group_merged)["CON", ] > 0],
  SCP = colnames(otu_table(group_merged))[otu_table(group_merged)["SCP", ] > 0],
  CP  = colnames(otu_table(group_merged))[otu_table(group_merged)["CP", ] > 0]
)

# 3. Create the Venn Diagram
p_venn <- ggVennDiagram(asv_list, label_alpha = 0, edge_lty = "dashed", edge_size = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") + # To match the 'count' scale in the image
  labs(title = "Distribution of ASVs among Groups",
       fill = "Count") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
p_venn

# Save the plot
ggsave("1_Rarefaction_curves/Venn_ASV_distribution.png", p_venn, width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

## 2.1. Estimate Richness

```{r}
setwd("~/Escritorio/R/2026_COPROFAGIA/coprofagia/2_Alpha_diversity")

richness <- estimate_richness(physeq_OF)
head(richness)
write.table(richness, file = "richness.tsv", sep = ",", quote = FALSE, row.names = T)

# Fix the factor order inside the phyloseq object before plotting
physeq_OF@sam_data$group <- factor(physeq_OF@sam_data$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# Plot richness
plot_richness(physeq_OF)

a_my_comparisons_group <- list( c("CON", "SCP"), c("CON", "CP"), c("SCP", "CP"))

symnum.args = list(cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1), symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns"))

plot_richness(physeq_OF, x = "group", color = "group", measures = c("Observed", "Chao1","Shannon"), title = "Alpha diversity indices of samples") + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"), breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"), breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP")) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=1, size=12)) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", comparisons = a_my_comparisons_group, label = "p.signif", symnum.args = symnum.args)
ggsave("alpha_diversity_group.svg", height = 7, width = 8, dpi = 300, device = "svg")

plot_richness(physeq_OF, x = "group", color = 'group', measures = c("Observed","Shannon"), title = "Alpha diversity indices of samples") + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"), breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02"), breaks = c("CON", "SCP", "CP")) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=1, size=12))
ggsave("alpha_diversity_group_without_NS.svg", height = 7, width = 6, dpi = 300, device = "svg")
```

## 2.2. Enhanced Alpha Diversity Plotting Script

```{r}
setwd("~/Escritorio/R/2026_COPROFAGIA/coprofagia/2_Alpha_diversity")

# 1. Define a professional color palette
# CON = Grey/Black, CP = Red, SCP = Blue
my_colors <- c("CON" = "#008B8B", "CP" = "#8A2BE2", "SCP" = "#D95F02")

# 2. Define statistical comparisons
a_my_comparisons_group <- list(c("CON", "SCP"), c("CON", "CP"), c("SCP", "CP"))

# 3. Create the optimized plot
p_alpha <- plot_richness(physeq_OF, x = "group", color = "group", 
                         measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon"), 
                         title = "Alpha Diversity Indices") + 
  # Use points + boxplot for better data distribution visibility
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = group), alpha = 0.2, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Scientific Theme Enhancements
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) +
  
  # Adjust text for clarity
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(), # Removes the grey boxes behind titles
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none", # Often better to remove legend if x-axis is labeled
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  ) #+
  
  # Statistical comparison with optimized label height
  # stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", 
                     #comparisons = a_my_comparisons_group, 
                     #label = "p.signif",
                     #step.increase = 0.1)
p_alpha

# 4. Save as high-resolution SVG
ggsave("alpha_diversity_high_level.svg", plot = p_alpha, height = 5, width = 8, dpi = 300)
```

## 2.5. Analysis of variance (ANOVA)

```{r}
anova.sh.group = aov(richness$Shannon ~ group, metadata)
summary_ANOVA_shannon_group = summary(anova.sh.group)
summary_ANOVA_shannon_group
capture.output(summary_ANOVA_shannon_group, file = "2_Alpha_diversity/ANOVA_Shannon_Group.txt")

anova.ch1.group = aov(richness$Chao1 ~ group, metadata)
summary_ANOVA_chao1_group = summary(anova.ch1.group)
summary_ANOVA_chao1_group
capture.output(summary_ANOVA_chao1_group, file = "2_Alpha_diversity/ANOVA_Chao1_Group.txt")
```

## 2.6. Tukey Honest Significant Differences (Tukey HSD)

```{r}
TukeyHSD_shannon_group
```

## 3.1. OTU-based metrics

```{r}
OTUs = physeq_OF@otu_table@.Data # To use the “group” column as the row names so that it will match our metadata
OTU_final = as.data.frame(t(OTUs)) #transpose # https://www.dataanalytics.org.uk/rotating-or-transposing-r-objects/#:~:text=Rotating%20or%20transposing%20R%20objects&text=That%20is%2C%20you%20transpose%20the,use%20the%20t()%20command.&text=The%20result%20of%20the%20t()%20command%20is%20always%20a%20matrix%20object.&text=You%20can%20also%20rotate%20a,table%20only%20has%202%20dimensions.
OTU_final
## In case you have to delete a column:
# OTU.clean = OTU[,-which(names(OTU) %in% c("label", "numOtus", "Group"))] # to remove the “label”, “numOTUs”, and “Group” columns as they are not OTU counts like the rest of the table
```

### 3.1.1. Ordination scatterplots

```{r}
# Bray-Curtis metric
BC.nmds = metaMDS(OTU_final, distance="bray", k=2, trymax=20) # calculate the nMDS values
# check the stress is lower than 0.2

## Plot the nMDS
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
### Create a blank plot for the NMDS
plot(BC.nmds, type="n", main="Bray-Curtis")
### Add the points colored by age
points(BC.nmds, display="sites", pch=20, col=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02")[metadata$group])
### Add a legend
legend(-0.7, 0.4, legend=c("CON","SCP","CP"), col=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02"), pch=20)
#### Save as "OTU_based_NMDS_BC_group.tiff"

# Jaccard metric 
## http://127.0.0.1:25357/graphics/plot_zoom_png?width=476&height=399
J.nmds = metaMDS(OTU_final, distance="jaccard", k=2, trymax=1000)

plot(J.nmds, type="n", main="Jaccard")
points(BC.nmds, display="sites", pch=20, col=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02")[metadata$group])
legend(-0.7, 0.4, legend=c("CON","SCP","CP"), col=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02"), pch=20)
#### Save as "OTU_based_NMDS_J_group.tiff"

# 3D plots
## Calculate the Bray-Curtis nMDS for 3-axis
BC.nmds.3D = metaMDS(OTU_final, distance="bray", k=3, trymax=1000)

### Extract x-y-z values for this nMDS
BCxyz = scores(BC.nmds.3D, display="sites")
#### This is a table that looks like 
BCxyz

group_factor <- factor(metadata$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))
plot_ly(x=BCxyz[,1], y=BCxyz[,2], z=BCxyz[,3], type="scatter3d", mode="markers", color=group_factor, colors=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02"))
##### Save as "3D_OTU_based_NMDS_BC_group.png"

J.nmds.3D = metaMDS(OTU_final, distance="jaccard", k=3, trymax=1000)
Jxyz = scores(J.nmds.3D, display="sites")
Jxyz
plot_ly(x=Jxyz[,1], y=Jxyz[,2], z=Jxyz[,3], type="scatter3d", mode="markers", color=group_factor, colors=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02"))
##### Save as "3D_OTU_based_NMDS_J_group.png"

## To create two separate 2D plots to show the 3D data
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
### Axis 1 and 2 (x and y)
plot(BCxyz[,1], BCxyz[,2], main="Bray-Curtis 1:2", pch=20, col=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02")[metadata$group])
legend(-0.6, 0.4, legend=c("CON","SCP","CP"), col=c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02"), pch=20)
### Axis 1 and 3 (x and z)
```

## 3.3. Statistically test beta-diversity

### 3.3.1. PERMANOVA (permutational analysis of variance)

```{r}
# Ordination scatterplots
## Calculate distance and save as a matrix
BC.dist=vegdist(OTU_final, distance="bray")
## Run PERMANOVA on distances
PERMANOVA_BC = adonis2(BC.dist ~ group, data = metadata, permutations = 1000)
PERMANOVA_BC
capture.output(PERMANOVA_BC, file = "3_Beta_diversity/PERMANOVA_BC.txt")

J.dist= vegdist(OTU_final, distance="jaccard")
PERMANOVA_J = adonis2(J.dist ~ group, data = metadata, permutations = 1000)
PERMANOVA_J
capture.output(PERMANOVA_J, file = "3_Beta_diversity/PERMANOVA_J.txt")


wUF.dist = UniFrac(physeq_OF, weighted=TRUE, normalized=TRUE)
PERMANOVA_wUF = adonis2(wUF.dist ~ group, data=metadata, permutations = 1000)
PERMANOVA_wUF
capture.output(PERMANOVA_wUF, file = "3_Beta_diversity/PERMANOVA_wUF.txt")

uwUF.dist = UniFrac(physeq_OF, weighted=FALSE, normalized=TRUE)
PERMANOVA_uwUF = adonis2(uwUF.dist ~ group, data=metadata, permutations = 1000)
PERMANOVA_uwUF
capture.output(PERMANOVA_uwUF, file = "3_Beta_diversity/PERMANOVA_uwUF.txt")
```

```{r}
ANOSIM_J_Group = anosim(J.dist, metadata$group, permutations = 1000)
ANOSIM_J_Group
capture.output(ANOSIM_J_Group, file = "3_Beta_diversity/ANOSIM_J_Group.txt")


ANOSIM_wUF_Group = anosim(wUF.dist, metadata$group, permutations = 1000)

ANOSIM_uwUF_Group
```

### 3.3.3. Beta dispersion

```{r}
disp.BC.group = betadisper(BC.dist, metadata$group)
test.disp.BC.group = permutest(disp.BC.group, pairwise=TRUE, permutations=1000)
```

## 3.4. Constrained Ordinations

```{r}
# Remove data points with missing metadata
erie_not_na <- physeq_OF %>%
  subset_samples(
    !is.na(group) 
  )

bray_not_na <- phyloseq::distance(physeq = erie_not_na, method = "unifrac")

# CAP ordinate
# An alternative (more PERMANOVA-like) would be to use a canonical analysis of principal coordinates (CAP) to find axes that best 
# discriminate among groups of interest (like a distance-based discriminant analysis) and then overlay Spearman rank correlation 
# vectors of species abundances with the 2 canonical axes. This is also a nice way of graphically looking at patterns.

cap_ord <- ordinate(
  physeq = erie_not_na, 
  method = "CAP",
  distance = bray_not_na,
  formula = ~ group
)

# CAP plot
cap_plot <- plot_ordination(
  physeq = erie_not_na, 
  ordination = cap_ord, 
  color = "group", 
  axes = c(1,2)
) + 
  aes(shape = group) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group), alpha = 0.7, size = 8) + 
  geom_point(colour = "grey90", size = 1.5) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02")) + theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("CAP1 [", round(cap_ord$CCA$eig[1]/sum(cap_ord$CCA$eig)*100, 1), "%]"),
    y = paste0("CAP2 [", round(cap_ord$CCA$eig[2]/sum(cap_ord$CCA$eig)*100, 1), "%]")
  )
cap_plot

# Now add the environmental variables as arrows
arrowmat <- vegan::scores(cap_ord, display = "bp")

# Add labels, make a data.frame
arrowdf <- data.frame(labels = rownames(arrowmat), arrowmat)

# Define the arrow aesthetic mapping
arrow_map <- aes(xend = CAP1, 
                 yend = CAP2, 
                 x = 0, 
                 y = 0, 
                 shape = NULL, 
                 color = NULL, 
                 label = labels)

label_map <- aes(x = 1.4 * CAP1, 
                 y = 1.4 * CAP2, 
                 shape = NULL, 
                 color = NULL, 
                 label = labels)

arrowhead = arrow(length = unit(0.02, "npc"))

# Make a new graphic
cap2_bray <- cap_plot +
  geom_segment(
    mapping = arrow_map, 
    size = .7, 
    data = arrowdf, 
    color = "gray", 
    arrow = arrowhead
  ) + 
  geom_text(
    mapping = label_map, 
    size = 7,  
    data = arrowdf, 
    show.legend = FALSE
  )
cap2_bray
ggsave(file="3_Beta_diversity/beta_diversity_cap_uwUF.svg", plot=cap2_bray, width=15, height=12, dpi = 300, limitsize =FALSE)
```

## 4.2. Plotting a heatmap (Option B)

```{r}
# 1. Load data
metadata <- read_q2metadata("metadata.tsv")
SVs_matrix <- physeq_OF@otu_table@.Data

# 2. Extract and Deep Clean Full Taxonomy
taxonomy_raw <- read_qza("taxa.qza")$data
taxonomy_df <- as.data.frame(taxonomy_raw)

# Clean the strings but keep the full path up to Genus
taxonomy_df$Full_Genus_Path <- sapply(strsplit(as.character(taxonomy_df$Taxon), ";"), function(x) {
  # We take up to 6 levels (Kingdom to Genus) and paste them back together
  path <- paste(x[1:min(length(x), 6)], collapse = ";")
  # Remove any double quotes to keep the labels clean
  gsub('"', '', path)
})

# 3. Manual Aggregation
combined_data <- merge(as.data.frame(SVs_matrix), 
                       taxonomy_df[, c("Feature.ID", "Full_Genus_Path")], 
                       by.x = "row.names", by.y = "Feature.ID")

taxasums <- combined_data %>%
  group_by(Full_Genus_Path) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
  # We use the full path as the row name for the heatmap labels
  column_to_rownames("Full_Genus_Path")

# 4. Generate and save Heatmap
taxa_heatmap(taxasums, metadata, "group", ntoplot = 30)

# Save with a slightly wider width to accommodate the longer names
ggsave("4_Heatmap/heatmap_group_full_path.tiff", 
       height = 8, width = 14, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
```

### 5.2.1. Phylum-level Sample Barplot with "Other"
```{r}
# 1. Filter low-count features (e.g., > 2 total reads across dataset)
prune.dat <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(phyloseq::taxa_sums(physeq_OF) > 2, physeq_OF)

# 2. Agglomerate at the Phylum level across the entire community
dat.aglo.phylum <- phyloseq::tax_glom(prune.dat, taxrank = "Phylum", NArm = FALSE)

# 3. Transform to true relative proportions (each sample sums exactly to 1.0 / 100%)
dat.rel.phylum <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(dat.aglo.phylum, function(x) x / sum(x))
df_s4 <- phyloseq::psmelt(dat.rel.phylum)

# 4. Clean taxonomic labels and handle missing values
df_s4$Phylum <- as.character(df_s4$Phylum)
df_s4$Phylum[is.na(df_s4$Phylum) | df_s4$Phylum == ""] <- "Unclassified"

# 5. Identify the top 10 most abundant phyla across all samples
top10_phyla <- df_s4 %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Phylum) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_abund = mean(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(mean_abund)) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Phylum)

# 6. Reassign remaining phyla to the "Other" category
df_s4 <- df_s4 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Phylum_Display = ifelse(Phylum %in% top10_phyla, Phylum, "Other"))

# Set legend order: Top 10 phyla followed by "Other"
phylum_order <- c(setdiff(top10_phyla, "Other"), "Other")
df_s4$Phylum_Display <- factor(df_s4$Phylum_Display, levels = phylum_order)

# Set facet group order
df_s4$group <- factor(df_s4$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# 7. Generate individual sample stacked bar chart
p_s4 <- ggplot(df_s4, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Phylum_Display)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.85) +
  facet_grid(~group, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1.005)) +

    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 10, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),

    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

print(p_s4)

# 8. Save figure
```

```{r}
dat.dataframe <- phyloseq::psmelt(dat.rel)
```

## 8.4. Bacterial Families with Significant Pairwise Differences

```{r}
# 1. Enforce the exact group factor levels order inside the phyloseq object
physeq_OF@sam_data$group <- factor(physeq_OF@sam_data$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# 2. Transform raw counts into Relative Abundance (%)
physeq_rel <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_OF, function(x) 100 * x / sum(x))

# 3. Taxonomically glom to Family level
physeq_fam <- tax_glom(physeq_rel, taxrank = "Family")

# 4. Melt to data frame for thorough statistical screening
df_all <- psmelt(physeq_fam)

# 5. Run Wilcoxon tests and keep only the exact pairs that are significant per family
pairwise_screening <- df_all %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  filter(sum(Abundance) > 0) %>% 
  do(tidy_test = pairwise.wilcox.test(.$Abundance, .$group, p.adjust.method = "none") %>% tidy()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unnest(tidy_test) %>%
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

## Extract only the unique names of families that passed the pairwise threshold
target_families <- unique(pairwise_screening$Family)

# 6. Checkpoint: Safeguard against empty sets
if(length(target_families) == 0) {
  stop("No bacterial families reached statistical significance in any pairwise comparison.")
}

# 7. Filter the phyloseq data
physeq_sub <- subset_taxa(physeq_fam, Family %in% target_families)
df_plot <- psmelt(physeq_sub)

# 8. Create a custom plotting function to apply targeted comparisons per facet
plot_list <- lapply(target_families, function(fam) {
  
  ## Filter data for this specific family
  df_fam <- filter(df_plot, Family == fam)
  
  ## Extract the specific significant pairs for THIS family only
  fam_sig_pairs <- pairwise_screening %>%
    filter(Family == fam) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(pair = list(c(group1, group2))) %>%
    pull(pair)
  
  ## Build the individual panel cleanly
  ggplot(df_fam, aes(x = group, y = Abundance, fill = group)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, color = "black", size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~Family, scales = "free_y") +
    
    ### Inject only the significant brackets for this panel
    stat_compare_means(
      comparisons = fam_sig_pairs, 
      label = "p.signif", 
      method = "wilcox.test",
      exact = FALSE,
      symnum.args = list(cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1), symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns"))
    ) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02")) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + # Clean labels for grid blending
    theme(
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold.italic", size = 11),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none" # Hide individual legends
    )
})

# 9. Assemble Proportionally in a Single Row
combined_panels <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list, nrow = 1, align = "h", axis = "tb")

dummy_plot <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = group, y = Abundance, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CON" = "#008B8B", "SCP" = "#8A2BE2", "CP" = "#D95F02")) +
  labs(fill = "Group") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right")
shared_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(dummy_plot)

## Final integration with y-axis label and main title
final_row_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  cowplot::ggdraw() + cowplot::draw_label("Relative Abundance (%)", angle = 90, fontface = "bold", size = 12),
  combined_panels,
  shared_legend,
  nrow = 1,
  rel_widths = c(0.05, 1, 0.15)
)

# 10. Save the layout
calculated_width <- length(target_families) * 3.8
ggsave("8_LDA/All_Pairwise_Significant_Families.tiff", final_row_plot, height = 5, width = calculated_width, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
```

## 8.5. Family Differential Abundance Info
```{r}
# 1. Enforce factor level ordering for experimental cohorts
physeq_OF@sam_data$group <- factor(physeq_OF@sam_data$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# 2. Transform raw counts to Relative Abundance (%)
physeq_rel <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_OF, function(x) 100 * x / sum(x))

# 3. Taxonomically agglomerate at the Family level
physeq_fam <- tax_glom(physeq_rel, taxrank = "Family")

# 4. Melt to long-format data frame
df_all <- psmelt(physeq_fam)

# 5. Extract total number of evaluated bacterial families (non-zero abundance)
evaluated_families <- df_all %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  filter(sum(Abundance) > 0) %>%
  summarise(Total_Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")

total_n_families <- nrow(evaluated_families)
cat("Total number of evaluated bacterial families:", total_n_families, "\n")

# 6. Execute pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests across all families
pairwise_tests <- df_all %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  filter(sum(Abundance) > 0) %>%
  do(tidy_test = pairwise.wilcox.test(.$Abundance, .$group, p.adjust.method = "none") %>% tidy()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unnest(tidy_test) %>%
  rename(
    Group1 = group1,
    Group2 = group2,
    Unadjusted_p_value = p.value
  ) %>%
  # Apply global False Discovery Rate (FDR / Benjamini-Hochberg) adjustment
  mutate(FDR_q_value = p.adjust(Unadjusted_p_value, method = "BH"))

# 7. Compute descriptive statistics (Median and IQR) per group
group_stats <- df_all %>%
  group_by(Family, group) %>%
  summarise(
    Median = median(Abundance),
    IQR_25 = quantile(Abundance, 0.25),
    IQR_75 = quantile(Abundance, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 8. Compute effect sizes (Median Difference between comparison pairs)
effect_sizes <- pairwise_tests %>%
  left_join(group_stats, by = c("Family" = "Family", "Group1" = "group")) %>%
  rename(Median_Group1 = Median, IQR25_Group1 = IQR_25, IQR75_Group1 = IQR_75) %>%
  left_join(group_stats, by = c("Family" = "Family", "Group2" = "group")) %>%
  rename(Median_Group2 = Median, IQR25_Group2 = IQR_25, IQR75_Group2 = IQR_75) %>%
  mutate(
    Comparison = paste(Group2, "vs", Group1),
    Median_Difference = Median_Group2 - Median_Group1
  ) %>%
  select(
    Family,
    Comparison,
    Median_Group2,
    IQR25_Group2,
    IQR75_Group2,
    Median_Group1,
    IQR25_Group1,
    IQR75_Group1,
    Median_Difference,
    Unadjusted_p_value,
    FDR_q_value
  ) %>%
  arrange(Family, Comparison)

# 9. Export comprehensive results for Supplementary Table S6
write.csv(effect_sizes, "Supplementary_Table_S6_Family_Differential_Abundance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## 8.6. Family Differential Abundance Info II
```{r}
# 1. Enforce factor level ordering for experimental cohorts
physeq_OF@sam_data$group <- factor(physeq_OF@sam_data$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))

# 2. Transform raw counts to Relative Abundance (%)
physeq_rel <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_OF, function(x) 100 * x / sum(x))

# 3. Taxonomically agglomerate at the Family level
physeq_fam <- tax_glom(physeq_rel, taxrank = "Family")

# 4. Melt phyloseq object to long-format data frame
df_all <- psmelt(physeq_fam)

# 5. Extract and print total number of evaluated bacterial families
evaluated_families <- df_all %>%

total_n_families <- nrow(evaluated_families)
cat("Total number of evaluated bacterial families:", total_n_families, "\n")

# 6. Execute pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and calculate FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg)
pairwise_tests <- df_all %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  filter(sum(Abundance) > 0) %>%
  do(tidy_test = pairwise.wilcox.test(.$Abundance, .$group, p.adjust.method = "none") %>% tidy()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unnest(tidy_test) %>%
  rename(Group1 = group1, Group2 = group2, p_raw = p.value) %>%
  mutate(p_adj_BH = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH"))

# 7. Compute descriptive metrics (Median and IQR) per group

  group_by(Family, group) %>%

    .groups = "drop"
  )

  rename(Median_G1 = Median, IQR25_G1 = IQR_25, IQR75_G1 = IQR_75) %>%
  left_join(group_stats, by = c("Family" = "Family", "Group2" = "group")) %>%

    `Median (IQR) Group 1 (%)` = sprintf("%.4f (%.4f–%.4f)", Median_G1, IQR25_G1, IQR75_G1),
    `Median (IQR) Group 2 (%)` = sprintf("%.4f (%.4f–%.4f)", Median_G2, IQR25_G2, IQR75_G2),
    `Effect Size (ΔMedian, %)` = round(Median_G1 - Median_G2, 4),
    `Unadjusted p-value (p_raw)` = round(p_raw, 4),
    `FDR-adjusted p-value (p_adj_BH)` = round(p_adj_BH, 4)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Bacterial Family`,
    `Comparison (Group 1 vs Group 2)`,
    `Median (IQR) Group 1 (%)`,
    `Median (IQR) Group 2 (%)`,
    `Effect Size (ΔMedian, %)`,
    `Unadjusted p-value (p_raw)`,
    `FDR-adjusted p-value (p_adj_BH)`
  ) %>%
  arrange(`Bacterial Family`, `Comparison (Group 1 vs Group 2)`)

# 9. Export formatted table to Excel (.xlsx) and CSV (.csv)
```

## 8.7. Family-Level Differential Abundance via ANCOM-BC2
# Purpose : Compositionally aware differential abundance testing across cohorts
# Required Packages: phyloseq, TreeSummarizedExperiment, ANCOMBC, S4Vectors
```{r}
# 1. Load the primary phyloseq package
library(phyloseq)

# 2. Agglomerate raw sequence counts at the Family level
# NOTE: Raw count data (not normalized percentages) are required for ANCOM-BC2
physeq_fam_raw <- phyloseq::tax_glom(physeq_OF, taxrank = "Family")

# 3. Extract the count matrix (taxa as rows, samples as columns)
raw_counts <- as(physeq_fam_raw@otu_table, "matrix")
if (!phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(physeq_fam_raw)) {
  raw_counts <- t(raw_counts)
}

# 4. Extract taxonomy and format family names as unique identifiers
tax_mat <- as(physeq_fam_raw@tax_table, "matrix")
fam_names <- as.character(tax_mat[, "Family"])
fam_names[is.na(fam_names) | fam_names == ""] <- "Unclassified_Family"
rownames(raw_counts) <- make.unique(fam_names)

# 5. Extract metadata and enforce factor levels
meta_df <- data.frame(
  group = as.character(physeq_fam_raw@sam_data$group),
  row.names = rownames(physeq_fam_raw@sam_data),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 6. Export input data to a temporary RDS file to ensure a clean R execution environment
saveRDS(list(counts = raw_counts, meta = meta_df), file = "ancombc_input_temp.rds")

# 7. Execute ANCOM-BC2 in an isolated background R session to avoid namespace conflicts
system2(
  command = R.home("bin/Rscript"),
  args = c("-e", shQuote('
    library(TreeSummarizedExperiment)
    library(ANCOMBC)
    library(S4Vectors)
    
    # Load prepared input data
    dat <- readRDS("ancombc_input_temp.rds")
    meta <- dat$meta
    meta$group <- factor(meta$group, levels = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"))
    
    # Construct TreeSummarizedExperiment object
    tse <- TreeSummarizedExperiment(
      assays = list(counts = dat$counts),
      colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(meta)
    )
    
    # Execute ANCOM-BC2 pairwise testing
    set.seed(1234)
    out <- ancombc2(
      data = tse,
      assay_name = "counts",
      tax_level = NULL,            # Input matrix is already agglomerated at family level
      fix_formula = "group",
      p_adj_method = "BH",
      prv_cut = 0.10,              # Prevalence threshold: present in >= 10% of samples
      group = "group",
      struc_zero = TRUE,           # Screen for structural zeros
      neg_lb = TRUE,               # Pseudo-count lower bound
      pairwise = TRUE,             # Multi-group pairwise comparisons
      verbose = FALSE
    )
    
    # Export full pairwise differential results to CSV
    write.csv(out$res_pair, "Supplementary Data S4. ANCOMBC2 Family Pairwise Results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("ANCOM-BC2 analysis completed successfully.\n")
  '))
)

# 8. Load and inspect results in the current session
if (file.exists("Supplementary Data S4. ANCOMBC2 Family Pairwise Results.csv")) {
  res_ancom <- read.csv("Supplementary Data S4. ANCOMBC2 Family Pairwise Results.csv")
  cat("Output Dimensions:", dim(res_ancom), "\n")
  print(head(res_ancom[, 1:7]))
}
```

# 9. Heat tree (Metacoder)

## 9.1. Generate the taxasums files per taxonomy level

```{r}
# Reference: 
# https://grunwaldlab.github.io/metacoder_documentation/example.html

# 1. Setup output directory
output_path_heattree <- "9_Heat_tree"
dir.create(output_path_heattree, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# 2. Load primary data
## Read the OTU matrix and force it into a standard data frame
otu_data <- as.data.frame(read_qza("filtered-table-genus.qza")$data) # or table-dada2.qza
tax_data <- read_qza("taxa.qza")$data                      

# 3. Synchronize and Merge
otu_data$Feature.ID <- rownames(otu_data)
combined_data <- merge(otu_data, tax_data[, c("Feature.ID", "Taxon")], by = "Feature.ID")

# 4. Manual Aggregation Function
# This bypasses Metacoder/Phyloseq bugs while preserving all hierarchical info
generate_taxasums <- function(data, depth) {
  data %>%
    # Split taxonomy string and rejoin up to the specified level
    mutate(Target_Taxon = sapply(strsplit(as.character(Taxon), ";"), function(x) {
      paste(x[1:min(length(x), depth)], collapse = ";")
    })) %>%
    # This cleans the taxon names specifically
    mutate(Target_Taxon = gsub('"', '', Target_Taxon)) %>%
    # Clean up the table for summation
    select(-Feature.ID, -Taxon) %>%
    group_by(Target_Taxon) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum)) %>%
    rename(OTU_ID = Target_Taxon)
}

# 5. Process and Export all 7 levels
# This keeps your sample headers exactly as they are
tax_levels <- list(Kingdom=1, Phylum=2, Class=3, Order=4, Family=5, Genus=6, Species=7)

for (level_name in names(tax_levels)) {
  result_table <- generate_taxasums(combined_data, tax_levels[[level_name]])
  
  # Remove any empty or NA rows
  result_table <- result_table[result_table$OTU_ID != "" & !is.na(result_table$OTU_ID), ]
  
  # Export to CSV without quotes in the final file
  file_name <- paste0("taxasums_", tolower(level_name), ".csv")
  write.csv(result_table, file.path(output_path, file_name), row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
}

message("---------------------------------------------------")
message("SUCCESS: 7 files generated in '9_Heat_tree'")
message("All quotes removed and taxonomy strings preserved.")
message("---------------------------------------------------")
```

```{r}
# 1. Print existing column names in diff_table for verification

tax_ranks <- taxon_ranks(obj)

# Add adjusted p-values if not already present

  raw_diff$wilcox_p_value_adj <- p.adjust(raw_diff$wilcox_p_value, method = "fdr")
}

# Attach taxon names and ranks safely
raw_diff$Taxon_Name <- as.character(tax_names[raw_diff$taxon_id])
raw_diff$Taxonomic_Rank <- as.character(tax_ranks[raw_diff$taxon_id])
raw_diff$Comparison <- paste(raw_diff$treatment_1, "vs", raw_diff$treatment_2)

# Standardize numeric outputs
diff_df <- raw_diff %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Taxon Name` = Taxon_Name,
    `Taxonomic Rank` = Taxonomic_Rank,
    `Comparison (Group 1 vs Group 2)` = Comparison,
    `Effect Size (Log2 Median Ratio)` = round(log2_median_ratio, 4),
    `Unadjusted p-value (p_raw)` = round(wilcox_p_value, 4),
    `FDR-adjusted p-value (p_adj_BH)` = round(wilcox_p_value_adj, 4)
  )

# Keep all key statistical columns cleanly
final_cols <- c(
  "Taxon Name",
  "Taxonomic Rank",

  "Effect Size (Log2 Median Ratio)",
  "Unadjusted p-value (p_raw)",

)

# If group-specific medians/means exist, append them

if (length(extra_num_cols) > 0) {
  diff_df[extra_num_cols] <- lapply(diff_df[extra_num_cols], function(x) round(x, 6))
  final_cols <- c(final_cols, extra_num_cols)
}

# 4. Export to Excel and CSV
```

# 10. Venn Diagrams
## 10.1. Option 1
```{r}
# 1. Directory and Data Preparation
output_path_venn <- "10_Venn_Diagram"
dir.create(output_path_venn, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Generate the Venn list from the phyloseq object and export text
vennlist_group <- get_vennlist(physeq_MF, factorNames="group")
capture.output(vennlist_group, file = "10_Venn_Diagram/VennList_Group.txt")

# 2. OTU Processing per Group
# Extract the taxonomy
OTUs_List <- physeq_MF@tax_table@.Data

# Function to clean and extract unique Genus names
process_otu_group <- function(otu_ids, tax_table) {
  tax_subset <- tax_table[otu_ids, "Genus"]
  tax_mat <- matrix(tax_subset)
  # Remove duplicates and "NA" strings often generated by QIIME2/phyloseq imports
  clean_tax <- tax_mat[!duplicated(tax_mat), ]
  clean_tax <- clean_tax[clean_tax != "NA" & !is.na(clean_tax)]
  return(data.frame(Genus = clean_tax))
}

CON <- process_otu_group(vennlist_group$`CON`, OTUs_List)
SCP <- process_otu_group(vennlist_group$`SCP`, OTUs_List)
CP  <- process_otu_group(vennlist_group$`CP`, OTUs_List)

# Merge and save the Genus matrix (using 'zoo' to handle uneven row numbers)
Venn_Matrix_Group <- data.frame(CP, cbind(zoo(, 1:max(nrow(CP), nrow(CON), nrow(SCP))), 
                                         as.zoo(CON), as.zoo(SCP)))
colnames(Venn_Matrix_Group) <- c("CP", "CON", "SCP")
write.csv(Venn_Matrix_Group, "10_Venn_Diagram/Venn_Matrix_Group.csv", row.names=FALSE)

# 3. Final Graphic Generation

# Disable log files
options(warn = -1) 

venn.plot <- venn.diagram(
  x = vennlist_group,
  category.names = c("CON", "SCP", "CP"),
  filename = "10_Venn_Diagram/Venn_Diagram_Group_FINAL.tiff",
  output = TRUE,
  
  # Circle Aesthetics
  fill = c("#008B8B", "#8A2BE2", "#D95F02"), # Distinct, professional colors
  alpha = 0.40,
  lty = "solid",
  lwd = 2,
  col = "black", # Border color
  
  # Intersection Numbers
  cex = 1.5,             # Size of the numbers inside circles
  fontface = "bold",
  fontfamily = "sans",
  
  # Category Label Settings
  cat.cex = 1.5,
  cat.fontface = "bold",
  cat.default.pos = "outer",
  cat.dist = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05),
  
  # Export Quality
  imagetype = "tiff",
  res = 300,             # High resolution for publication
  height = 2500, 
  width = 2500,
  units = "px",
  compression = "lzw",
  bg = "white"
)

# 4. Export Partitions (Useful for supplementary tables)
getven_group <- get.venn.partitions(vennlist_group)
getven_clean <- data.frame(lapply(getven_group, as.character), stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
write.csv(getven_clean, "10_Venn_Diagram/Venn_Partitions_Group.csv")

message("Process complete. Check the '10_Venn_Diagram' folder for the final TIFF with numbers.")
```
